save_dialog_title.location: Results → Grid context menu → Save as Snapshot: title of the dialog that asks for a name before saving the current result set for later reopening.

save_name_required.location: Results → Grid context menu → Save as Snapshot dialog: inline error shown when Save is clicked with an empty or blank name field.

saving_reading_rows.location: Results → Grid caption strip: progress note above the grid while a large disk-paged result is read back before saving it as a snapshot; {row_count} is how many rows are being read.
saving_reading_rows.value: Saving snapshot — reading {row_count} rows from disk…

store_busy.location: Results → Save as Snapshot dialog: inline error shown when the snapshot store is locked by another save in progress and cannot accept this one right now.

truncated_suffix.location: Tools → Result Snapshots dialog → List row: marker inserted right after the row count in a snapshot’s subtitle when the result had more rows than the snapshot limit kept. Starts with a space.

open_failed_rows_on_disk.location: Results → Messages tab: message added when a large result’s temporary disk file cannot be reopened after the query; {result_number} is the result set number, {file_path} where the rows remain.
open_failed_rows_on_disk.value: Result {result_number}: spill file could not be opened; rows kept on disk at {file_path}

open_failed_rows_unavailable.location: Results → Error banner: error shown above the results when a large result’s temporary disk file cannot be reopened, so that result set’s rows cannot be displayed; {result_number} is its number.
open_failed_rows_unavailable.value: Result {result_number}: spill file could not be opened; its rows are unavailable

page_read_failed.location: Results → Messages tab: error message added when scrolling a large disk-paged result fails to read the next page of rows from its temporary file.
page_read_failed.value: Error: could not read this page of the result from disk. The file may have been removed or is unreadable.

failed.location: Results → Messages: notice shown when the rows behind a double-clicked pivot cell or clicked chart mark could not be collected because the large result's file on disk could not be read or written.
failed.value: Couldn't show the matching rows because the result file couldn't be read.

progress.location: Results → grid caption strip: progress shown while SQLLY collects the rows behind a double-clicked pivot cell or clicked chart mark from a large result kept on disk; {percent} is a whole percent.

clear_filters_tooltip.location: Results → Stacked layout → Result card header: tooltip on the filter-with-X button that removes all row filters from that result set; enabled only when filters are applied.

clear_grouping_tooltip.location: Results → Stacked layout → Result card header: tooltip on the grouping-with-X button that removes column grouping from that result set; enabled only when grouping is active.

clear_sort_tooltip.location: Results → Stacked layout → Result card header: tooltip on the sort-arrows-with-X button that removes the column sort from that result set; enabled only when a sort is applied.

filter_rows_tooltip.location: Results → Stacked layout → Result card header: tooltip on the funnel button that opens the filter builder to filter that result set’s rows; the ellipsis signals a dialog opens.

row_count.location: Results → Stacked layout → Result card header: dim row total shown after the result set’s name and edit icon; {row_count} is the number of rows in that result set.

copy_sql_button.location: Results → Tab strip → Staged-change controls: small button, after Preview SQL, shown while grid edits are pending; copies the generated INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE script for the pending changes to the clipboard.

copy_sql_tooltip.location: Results → Tab strip → Staged-change controls: tooltip on the Copy as SQL button explaining that it copies the script for the not-yet-saved grid changes to the clipboard.
copy_sql_tooltip.value: Copy the pending change script to the clipboard

count_summary.location: Results → Tab strip → Staged-change controls: dim summary text before the Undo button while edits are pending; {edited_count}, {inserted_count}, {deleted_count} are the numbers of edited, newly added and deleted rows.

discard_button.location: Results → Tab strip → Staged-change controls: last button in the row, after Save Changes; throws away all pending grid edits, inserts and deletes without writing them to the database.

newer_bridge_required.location: Results → Tab strip → Staged-change controls: warning text beside the change summary, shown when the connection runs through an older relay bridge that cannot save staged edits; Save Changes is disabled.

no_changes_to_copy.location: Results → Messages tab: message added when the user clicks Copy as SQL (or runs the copy command) but there are no staged grid changes to turn into a script.

no_keyed_rows_for_delete.location: Results → Messages tab: error shown when staging a delete for selected grid rows fails because none of them has a primary key value that identifies the row to delete.
no_keyed_rows_for_delete.value: None of the selected rows have a primary key that can be staged for delete.

preview_sql_button.location: Results → Tab strip → Staged-change controls: small button after Redo; opens the Preview SQL output tab showing the script that Save Changes would run for the pending edits.

redo_button.location: Results → Tab strip → Staged-change controls: small button after Undo, shown while edits are pending; re-applies the most recently undone staged grid change (verb, command label).

resolve_other_result_first.location: Results → Messages tab: plural message shown when the user tries to edit, insert or delete rows in one result set while several changes are pending in another; {change_count} is the pending change count, {result_number} the result set number.
resolve_other_result_first.value: Save or discard the {change_count} pending change(s) on result {result_number} first

resolve_other_result_first_one.location: Results → Messages tab: singular variant shown when exactly one change is pending in another result set and the user tries to stage an edit in a different one; {change_count} is 1, {result_number} is that result set number.
resolve_other_result_first_one.value: Save or discard the {change_count} pending change on result {result_number} first

save_button.location: Results → Tab strip → Staged-change controls: button after Transform; writes all pending grid edits, inserts and deletes to the database in one batch (disabled when an older relay bridge cannot save).

select_row_first.location: Results → Messages tab: message shown when the user asks to stage a delete of grid rows but no row is selected or the result set is not editable.

sql_copied.location: Results → Messages tab: confirmation logged after Copy as SQL puts the staged-change script on the clipboard; {change_count} is the total number of pending edits, inserts and deletes.
sql_copied.value: Copied the SQL for {change_count} staged change(s) to the clipboard

transform_button.location: Results → Tab strip → Staged-change controls: dropdown button after Copy as SQL that opens a menu of text transforms (such as changing case) to apply to every staged string value; verb, short space.

transform_no_plain_text_changes.location: Results → Messages tab: message after choosing a Transform menu item that changed nothing; {transform_name} is the chosen transform; explains JSON, XML, enum and SET columns are skipped.
transform_no_plain_text_changes.value: {transform_name}: no staged plain-text value changed (JSON, XML, enum, and SET columns are left alone)

transform_tooltip.location: Results → Tab strip → Staged-change controls: tooltip on the Transform dropdown button explaining it applies a chosen text macro to every pending string value.
transform_tooltip.value: Apply a text macro to every staged string value

transform_values_updated.location: Results → Messages tab: confirmation after a Transform menu item rewrote pending values; {transform_name} is the chosen transform, {changed_count} the number of staged values it changed.

undo_button.location: Results → Tab strip → Staged-change controls: first button after the change summary, shown while edits are pending; reverts the most recent staged grid change (verb, command label).

auto_refresh_tooltip.location: Results → Status bar: tooltip on the auto-refresh interval dropdown, shown for read-only SELECT queries; explains the query re-runs on the chosen timer and pauses while hidden or running.
auto_refresh_tooltip.value: Re-run this query on a timer. Pauses while the tab is hidden or a run is in progress.

calculate_total_rows.location: Results → Status bar: link beside the “Result N: rows” count, shown for a single finished result set; runs a separate count query to show the full number of rows the query would return.

calculate_total_rows_tooltip.location: Results → Status bar: tooltip on the Calculate total rows link explaining it runs COUNT(*) for the query and that TOP/LIMIT caps in the statement still apply to the total.
calculate_total_rows_tooltip.value: Run COUNT(*) for this query. Statement caps (TOP / LIMIT) are included in the total.

cancel_count_button.location: Results → Status bar: small button after the “counting…” text, shown while the total row count query runs; stops that count query (not the main query).

counting_rows.location: Results → Status bar: progress text shown in place of the Calculate total rows link while the COUNT(*) total row query is still running; lowercase fragment after the row count.

first_response_time.location: Results → Status bar → Detailed timing: label for the time until the server first responded, shown when detailed query timing is enabled; {duration} is the formatted time.

first_response_tooltip.location: Results → Status bar → Detailed timing: tooltip on the “First” timing explaining it measures query start to first server response, minus network latency when Subtract is ticked.
first_response_tooltip.value: Time from query start to first server response (latency subtracted if enabled)

grid_zoom.location: Results → Status bar: zoom indicator shown only when the results grid is zoomed away from 100%; double-clicking it resets the zoom; {zoom_percent} is the current zoom percentage.

latency_time.location: Results → Status bar → Detailed timing: label for the measured network round-trip time of the connection, shown when detailed timing is on; {milliseconds} is the latency in milliseconds.

latency_tooltip.location: Results → Status bar → Detailed timing: tooltip on the Latency label explaining it is the round-trip time of a SELECT 1 sent on connect, used as baseline network latency.
latency_tooltip.value: Round-trip time for SELECT 1 on connect — baseline network latency

paint_time.location: Results → Status bar → Detailed timing: label for how long the app took to draw the results after the query finished, shown when detailed timing is on; {duration} is the time.

paint_time_tooltip.location: Results → Status bar → Detailed timing: tooltip on the Paint timing explaining it is the time spent rendering the results in the interface once the query completed.
paint_time_tooltip.value: Time to render results in the UI after completion

query_running_elapsed.location: Results → Status bar: live text shown while a query is still executing, counting up the elapsed time; {elapsed_time} is the running duration.

query_time.location: Results → Status bar → Detailed timing: label for the server-side execution time reported by the database, shown when detailed timing is on; {duration} is the time.

query_time_tooltip.location: Results → Status bar → Detailed timing: tooltip on the Query timing label explaining it is the execution time as reported by the database server itself.
query_time_tooltip.value: Server-side execution time reported by the database

result_row_count.location: Results → Status bar: row count shown for each returned result set; {result_number} is the result set number (1, 2, …) and {row_count} the number of rows received.

rows_affected.location: Results → Status bar: count shown for a statement that returned no rows but changed data (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE); {result_number} is the result number, {row_count} the rows affected.

server_total_time.location: Results → Status bar → Detailed timing: label for the combined server time (first response plus execution), shown when detailed timing is on; {duration} is the time.

server_total_tooltip.location: Results → Status bar → Detailed timing: tooltip on the Server timing label explaining it is the first-response time plus the server execution time.

shown_of_total_rows.location: Results → Status bar: row count shown after Calculate total rows finishes; {result_number} is the result number, {shown_rows} the rows loaded in the grid, {total_rows} the full count.

subtract_latency.location: Results → Status bar → Detailed timing: checkbox label after the Latency value; when ticked, the measured network latency is subtracted from the displayed timings (verb, very short).

total_unavailable.location: Results → Status bar: link text shown in place of the total row count when the COUNT(*) query failed; hovering it shows the error from the database.

wall_time.location: Results → Status bar → Detailed timing: label for total user-perceived time (server time plus paint), shown when detailed timing is on; {duration} is the time; “Wall” as in wall-clock.

wall_time_tooltip.location: Results → Status bar → Detailed timing: tooltip on the Wall timing label explaining it is Server total plus Paint time, the full time the user waited.
wall_time_tooltip.value: Server Total + Paint — total user-perceived time

auto_existing_note.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: warning-colored note beside the Format picker when Auto detected an encoded or compressed value whose decode summary already names the format; “Auto:” prefixes that summary ({decode_note}).

auto_format_and_note.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: note shown when Auto detected an encoded, compressed or serialized value; {format_name} is the detected format (e.g. gzip) and {decode_note} the decoder’s remark, joined by a middle dot.

auto_format_only.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: note shown when Auto detected an encoded, compressed or serialized format and decoded it without further remarks; {format_name} is that format, e.g. “Auto: MessagePack”.

auto_window_title.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar: title at the left of the toolbar while the Format picker is on Auto; {kind_name} is the detected content kind (JSON, XML, Binary, Image, Geometry) and {column_name} the result column.

base64_empty.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when Base64 is picked but the value is empty or only whitespace; fills {error} in the “not decodable as …, showing the hex dump” warning.

base64_invalid.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when the value is text but no standard or URL-safe Base64 alphabet decodes it; fills {error} in the “not decodable as …, showing the hex dump” warning.

base64_not_ascii.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when Base64 is picked but the value’s bytes are not plain text, so they cannot be Base64; fills {error} in the “not decodable as …, showing the hex dump” warning.

binary_title.location: Results → Value viewer: content-kind name for raw binary values shown as a hex dump; used as {kind_name} in the viewer window title and toolbar title, before an em dash and the column name.

copy_button.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar: accent pill button at the right end of the toolbar that copies the whole displayed text (pretty-printed value or hex dump) to the clipboard.

decode_and_persistence_notes.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: combined warning shown when a picked format both produced a decode note ({decode_note}) and could not be remembered on disk ({persistence_error}); joined by a middle dot.

decode_failed_fallback.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: warning shown when the format picked in the Format menu cannot decode the value; {format_name} is that format, {error} the decoder’s reason; the hex dump is shown instead.
decode_failed_fallback.value: not decodable as {format_name} ({error}) — showing the hex dump

decode_note.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: note after decoding a Base64 or compressed value; {outer_format} is the picked format, {inner_format} what was found inside (JSON, XML, text, binary…), {byte_sizes} the before → after byte counts.

decoded_byte_sizes.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: byte-size fragment inside the decode note’s parentheses; {outer_bytes} is the encoded size and {inner_bytes} the decoded size, both with thousands separators.

decoded_size_cap.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: noun phrase naming the decoding size limit, inserted as {size_cap} into “… expands past …” and “… refuses it” reasons; {megabytes} is the limit in MB (16). Keep it a phrase that reads after “past”.

decoder_expands_past_cap.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when decompressing (gzip, zstd, LZ4, zlib or raw deflate) grows beyond the size limit; {decoder} is the decompressor name, {size_cap} the “the 16 MB cap” phrase; fills {error} in the “not decodable as …, showing the hex dump” warning.

decoder_read_failed.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when a decompressor reports an error while reading the stream; {decoder} is the decompressor name (zstd, LZ4, zlib, raw deflate…) and {error} its technical message.

deflate_empty.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when deflate is picked in the Format menu but the value has no bytes at all; fills {error} in the “not decodable as …, showing the hex dump” warning.

detached_window_title.location: Results → Value viewer window: operating-system title bar text of the separate viewer window opened from a results cell; {kind_name} is the content kind (JSON, XML, Binary, Image, Geometry), {column_name} the column.

format_auto.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format menu: first option and default format, which auto-detects the value (JSON, XML, compressed, serialized…); also fills {format_name} in the “Format: …” picker label.

format_java_serialized.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format menu: option in the serialized group that reads the value as a Java object serialization stream (summary of class names and strings); also used as a format name in notes.

format_php_serialized.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format menu: option in the serialized group that reads the value as PHP serialize() output and shows it as a tree; also used as a format name in notes and titles.

format_picker_label.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar: label of the dropdown button that opens the Format menu; {format_name} is the currently selected display format (Auto, UTF-8, JSON, Hex, gzip…).

format_picker_tooltip.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar: tooltip on the “Format: …” dropdown button, explaining that the picked format only changes how the value is displayed and never alters the stored data.
format_picker_tooltip.value: Show this value in a chosen format. Decoding is presentation only; the stored bytes never change.

format_window_title.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar: title at the left of the toolbar when a format other than Auto is picked; {format_name} is the picked format and {column_name} the result column.

geometry_title.location: Results → Value viewer: content-kind name for spatial (geometry/geography) values drawn as a sketch; used as {kind_name} in the viewer window title and toolbar title.

gzip_claimed_size_exceeds_cap.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when a gzip value’s trailer announces an uncompressed size over the limit, refused before inflating; {claimed_bytes} is that size, {size_cap} the “the 16 MB cap” phrase.
gzip_claimed_size_exceeds_cap.value: the gzip trailer claims {claimed_bytes} bytes; {size_cap} refuses it

gzip_missing_header.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when gzip is picked but the value does not start with the gzip magic bytes 1f 8b (or is too short); fills {error} in the “not decodable as …, showing the hex dump” warning.

gzip_unknown_method.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when a gzip header names a compression method other than deflate; {method} is the method number read from the header; fills {error} in the “not decodable as …, showing the hex dump” warning.

hex_search_placeholder.location: Results → Structured Data Viewer → hex constructor: search-field placeholder “Search” in the binary hex-dump toolbar.

hex_truncated_note.location: Results → Value viewer → Hex dump: line appended after the last row of a hex dump longer than 64 KB, starting on a new line; {hidden_bytes} is how many bytes are omitted, {total_bytes} the value’s full size.

image_fit_button.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Image zoom: segmented button beside “100%” that scales an image cell to fit the window; shown only for image values.

image_search_placeholder.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar: placeholder of the search box created for image values (the box is only displayed in Tree mode, so it is rarely seen); short noun or verb “Search”.

image_size_label.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar: dim label at the right of the toolbar for image values; {image_format} is the image type (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP) and {byte_count} the file size in bytes.

image_title.location: Results → Value viewer: content-kind name for image values (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP) shown as a picture; used as {kind_name} in the viewer window title and toolbar title.

inside_binary.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: word filled into {inner_format} of the decode note when the decoded bytes are neither text nor a recognized format, so they are shown as a hex dump; lowercase noun.

inside_text.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: word filled into {inner_format} of the decode note when the decoded bytes are plain text (not JSON, XML or a serialized format); lowercase noun.

invalid_json_note.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: warning shown when JSON is picked in the Format menu but the value does not parse as JSON; the text is shown unformatted instead.
invalid_json_note.value: not valid JSON — showing the raw text

invalid_yaml_note.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: warning shown when YAML is picked in the Format menu but the value does not parse as a YAML mapping or list; the text is shown unformatted instead.
invalid_yaml_note.value: not valid YAML — showing the raw text

preview_mode_button.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar: segment of the Preview/Raw toggle shown for Markdown values; shows the Markdown rendered.

edit_button.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar: button shown for a decompressed (gzip, zlib, deflate, zstd, LZ4, MySQL COMPRESS) value; opens an editor on the decompressed text.

edit_tooltip.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Edit button: tooltip; {format_name} is the compression the edited text will be packed back into (e.g. gzip).
edit_tooltip.value: Edit the decompressed text, then stage it re-compressed as {format_name}

stage_button.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar (while editing a decompressed value): button that re-compresses the edited text and stages it as a pending cell change; {format_name} is the compression (e.g. gzip).

cancel_edit_button.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar (while editing a decompressed value): button that closes the editor without staging anything.

recompress_staged.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar: status after an edited value was re-compressed and staged as a pending grid change; {format_name} is the compression (e.g. gzip).
recompress_staged.value: Staged, re-compressed as {format_name} — review and save it from the results grid

recompress_unknown_framing.location: Results → Value viewer and Redis Key View: reason the Edit button is unavailable — the exact compression packaging of the value could not be identified, so it is never re-compressed.
recompress_unknown_framing.value: Can't tell exactly how this value was compressed, so it can't be edited and re-compressed

recompress_not_text.location: Results → Value viewer and Redis Key View: reason the Edit button is unavailable — what is inside the compressed value is binary data, not text.
recompress_not_text.value: The decompressed value isn't text, so it can't be edited here

recompress_failed.location: Results → Value viewer and Redis Key View: error when packing an edited value back into its compression fails; {format_name} is the compression (e.g. gzip), {error} the reason.

recompress_verify_failed.location: Results → Value viewer: reason filled into {error} of the re-compression error when the packed value did not unpack to the edited text (nothing is staged).
recompress_verify_failed.value: the result didn't decompress back to the edited text

message_picker_label.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar: Protobuf message-type menu button label; {message} is the chosen message type (e.g. shop.Person) or the 'none' choice.

message_picker_none.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Message menu: choice that decodes the Protobuf value without a schema, by field number.

message_picker_tooltip.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar: tooltip of the Protobuf Message menu.
message_picker_tooltip.value: Decode with a message type from your Protobuf schemas (Settings ▸ Results ▸ Protobuf Schemas)

protobuf_schema_note.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: shown when a Protobuf value was decoded with a registered schema; {message} is the message type.

protobuf_schema_unknown_fields_note.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: shown when a Protobuf value decoded with a schema also carries fields the schema doesn't define; {message} is the message type, {field_numbers} a comma-separated list of field numbers.
protobuf_schema_unknown_fields_note.value: decoded as {message} · fields not in the schema: {field_numbers}

protobuf_schema_mismatch_note.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: shown when the chosen Protobuf message type doesn't fit the value, which is then shown by field number; {message} is the message type, {error} the reason.

protobuf_schemas_store_blocked.location: Results → Value viewer and Settings → Protobuf Schemas: error when the saved schema settings file can't be read, so changes are kept for this session only; {error} is the reason.
protobuf_schemas_store_blocked.value: Protobuf schema settings can't be saved (the settings file is unreadable): {error}

protobuf_schemas_save_failed.location: Results → Value viewer and Settings → Protobuf Schemas: error when writing the schema settings file fails; {error} is the reason.
protobuf_schemas_save_failed.value: Couldn't save the Protobuf schema settings: {error}

protobuf_schema_read_failed.location: Settings → Protobuf Schemas and Results → Value viewer: error when a .proto file or descriptor set can't be read or compiled; {path} is the file, {error} the compiler's reason.

protobuf_schema_no_messages.location: Settings → Protobuf Schemas: reason filled into {error} when an added schema file defines no message types.

protobuf_schema_missing.location: Results → Value viewer: reason filled into {error} of the mismatch note when the schema of the chosen message type was removed from Settings.
protobuf_schema_missing.value: its schema is no longer registered

protobuf_message_missing.location: Results → Value viewer: reason filled into {error} of the mismatch note when the schema no longer defines the chosen message type; {message} is its name.
protobuf_message_missing.value: the schema has no message named {message}

protobuf_schema_no_known_fields.location: Results → Value viewer: reason filled into {error} of the mismatch note when none of the value's fields belong to the chosen message type.
protobuf_schema_no_known_fields.value: none of the value's fields are in this message

invalid_utf8_note.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: warning shown when the value is displayed as UTF-8 text but contains invalid byte sequences, which appear as replacement characters.
invalid_utf8_note.value: not valid UTF-8 — lossy replacement shown

java_missing_header.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when Java serialization is picked but the value lacks the stream magic bytes ac ed; fills {error} in the “not decodable as …, showing the hex dump” warning.

java_summary_note.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: note shown after reading a Java serialization stream, warning that the tree lists only class names and strings because field values cannot be decoded without the classes.
java_summary_note.value: class names and strings only — field values are not decoded

java_unknown_stream_version.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when a Java serialization stream has an unsupported version; {version} is the version found and {supported_version} the only one understood (5).

lz4_claimed_size_exceeds_cap.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when an LZ4 block’s leading size prefix announces more than the limit, refused before decompressing; {claimed_bytes} is that size, {size_cap} the “the 16 MB cap” phrase.
lz4_claimed_size_exceeds_cap.value: the LZ4 block size prefix claims {claimed_bytes} bytes; {size_cap} refuses it

lz4_decode_failed.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when decompressing a size-prefixed LZ4 block fails; {error} is the decompressor’s technical message.

lz4_missing_header.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when LZ4 is picked but the value has no LZ4 frame magic bytes and is under 4 bytes, too short to be a size-prefixed block.
lz4_missing_header.value: no LZ4 frame header (04 22 4d 18) and too short for a block

messagepack_decode_failed.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: MessagePack decoder error passed through unchanged as the reason; {error} is the technical message. Usually kept as just the placeholder.

messagepack_expected_extension.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: noun phrase completing a MessagePack type error of the form “invalid type: …, expected …” when an extension value was expected; reads after “expected”.

messagepack_expected_extension_data.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: noun phrase completing a MessagePack type error “…, expected …” when an extension’s data bytes were expected; reads after “expected”.

messagepack_expected_value.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: noun phrase completing a MessagePack type error “invalid type: …, expected …” when any value was expected at that point; reads after “expected”.

messagepack_extension_missing_data.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when a MessagePack extension entry has a type code but no data bytes; fills {error} in the “not decodable as …, showing the hex dump” warning.

messagepack_extension_missing_type.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when a MessagePack extension entry is missing its type code; fills {error} in the “not decodable as …, showing the hex dump” warning.

messagepack_trailing_bytes.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when the value holds extra bytes after one complete MessagePack value; {byte_count} is the number of leftover bytes.
messagepack_trailing_bytes.value: {byte_count} trailing bytes after the first MessagePack value

nested_decode_note.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: decode note variant shown when the decoded bytes are themselves compressed again; like the plain note, plus {nested_format}, the inner compression that is deliberately not decoded a second time.
nested_decode_note.value: {outer_format} → {inner_format} ({byte_sizes}; the nested {nested_format} stream inside is not decompressed again)

php_array_key_invalid.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: PHP serialize reason used when an array entry’s key is itself an array; {byte_offset} is the key’s byte position; PHP only allows integer and string keys.
php_array_key_invalid.value: key at byte {byte_offset} is an array — only integers and strings are keys

php_boolean_key_invalid.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: PHP serialize reason used when an array entry’s key is a boolean; {byte_offset} is the key’s byte position; PHP only allows integer and string keys.
php_boolean_key_invalid.value: key at byte {byte_offset} is a boolean — only integers and strings are keys

php_bytes_truncated.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: PHP serialize reason used when a string’s declared bytes extend past the end of the value; {byte_count} is the declared length, {byte_offset} where the string starts.
php_bytes_truncated.value: {byte_count} bytes at byte {byte_offset} run past the end

php_delimiter_missing.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: PHP serialize reason used when an expected separator character never appears; {delimiter} is the quoted character (e.g. “;” or “:”), {byte_offset} where the search began.

php_entry_count_exceeds_remaining.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: PHP serialize reason used when an array or object claims more entries than the remaining bytes could hold; {entry_count} claimed entries, {byte_offset} position, {remaining_bytes} bytes left.
php_entry_count_exceeds_remaining.value: {entry_count} entries claimed at byte {byte_offset} with only {remaining_bytes} bytes left

php_invalid_integer.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: PHP serialize reason used when a number field (integer or length) cannot be parsed as an integer; {byte_offset} is its byte position.

php_length_exceeds_remaining.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: PHP serialize reason used when a string length is larger than the bytes left; {claimed_bytes} is the declared length, {byte_offset} its position, {remaining_bytes} what remains.
php_length_exceeds_remaining.value: length {claimed_bytes} at byte {byte_offset} is more than the {remaining_bytes} bytes left

php_negative_length.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: PHP serialize reason used when a string or array length field is negative; {byte_offset} is the byte position of that length.

php_nesting_exceeded.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: PHP serialize reason used when arrays or objects nest deeper than the safety limit; {maximum_depth} is that limit (128 levels).

php_null_key_invalid.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: PHP serialize reason used when an array entry’s key is null; {byte_offset} is the key’s byte position; PHP only allows integer and string keys.
php_null_key_invalid.value: key at byte {byte_offset} is null — only integers and strings are keys

php_object_key_invalid.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: PHP serialize reason used when an array entry’s key is an object or binary string; {byte_offset} is the key’s byte position; only integers and strings are keys.
php_object_key_invalid.value: key at byte {byte_offset} is an object or binary string — only integers and strings are keys

php_trailing_bytes.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: PHP serialize reason used when extra bytes follow one complete serialized value; {byte_count} is the number of leftover bytes.

php_unexpected_byte.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: PHP serialize reason used when a specific punctuation character was required but another was found; {expected} and {actual} are the quoted characters, {byte_offset} the position.

php_unexpected_end.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: PHP serialize reason used when the value ends in the middle of a serialized item; {byte_offset} is the position where more bytes were needed.

php_unexpected_tag.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: PHP serialize reason used when a type letter is not one PHP serialize uses; {tag_hex} is the byte in hex, {tag_character} the quoted character, {byte_offset} its position.

pickle_data_truncated.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Python pickle reason used when an instruction’s declared data runs past the end; {opcode} is the pickle opcode name, {byte_offset} its position, {claimed_bytes} the declared length.
pickle_data_truncated.value: {opcode} at byte {byte_offset} claims {claimed_bytes} bytes, past the end

pickle_line_unterminated.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Python pickle reason used when a text-line opcode has no newline before the value ends; {opcode} is the opcode name and {byte_offset} its position.
pickle_line_unterminated.value: {opcode} at byte {byte_offset} has no line end

pickle_missing_header.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Python pickle reason used when the value does not begin with a PROTO opcode (bytes 80 xx); explains only protocol 2 and later have one, so older pickles cannot be read.
pickle_missing_header.value: no pickle PROTO header (80 xx) — only protocol 2 and later carry one

pickle_opcode_truncated.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Python pickle reason used when an instruction’s fixed-size argument extends past the end of the value; {opcode} is the opcode name and {byte_offset} its position.
pickle_opcode_truncated.value: {opcode} at byte {byte_offset} runs past the end

pickle_summary_note.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: note shown after reading a Python pickle, warning that the tree is only a list of its instructions (opcodes) and the original Python object is not reconstructed.
pickle_summary_note.value: opcode summary only — the object is not rebuilt

pickle_trailing_bytes.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Python pickle reason used when bytes remain after the STOP instruction that ends a pickle; {byte_count} is the number of leftover bytes; STOP is an opcode name, not translated.

pickle_unknown_opcode.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Python pickle reason used when a byte is not a known pickle instruction; {opcode} is the byte in hex (e.g. 0xff) and {byte_offset} its position.

pickle_unknown_protocol.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Python pickle reason used when the header names a protocol number outside 1–5; {protocol} is the number found.

protobuf_empty.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when Protobuf is picked but the value has no bytes at all; fills {error} in the “not decodable as …, showing the hex dump” warning.

protobuf_field_truncated.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Protobuf reason used when a length-delimited field claims more bytes than remain; {field_number} is the field, {claimed_bytes} its declared length, {byte_offset} where its data starts.
protobuf_field_truncated.value: field {field_number} claims {claimed_bytes} bytes at byte {byte_offset}, past the end

protobuf_fixed32_truncated.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Protobuf reason used when a 4-byte fixed-width field (fixed32 is a technical term) runs past the end; {byte_offset} is where it starts.
protobuf_fixed32_truncated.value: fixed32 at byte {byte_offset} runs past the end

protobuf_fixed64_truncated.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Protobuf reason used when an 8-byte fixed-width field (fixed64 is a technical term) runs past the end; {byte_offset} is where it starts.
protobuf_fixed64_truncated.value: fixed64 at byte {byte_offset} runs past the end

protobuf_group_unsupported.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Protobuf reason used when a field uses the deprecated start-group/end-group wire type, which the viewer does not read; {field_number} is the field, {byte_offset} its position.
protobuf_group_unsupported.value: deprecated group wire type on field {field_number} at byte {byte_offset}

protobuf_invalid_field.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Protobuf reason used when a field tag has number 0 or above the allowed maximum; {field_number} is the number found and {byte_offset} the tag’s position.

protobuf_invalid_wire_type.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Protobuf reason used when a field tag carries a wire type that does not exist (6 or 7); {wire_type} is that number and {byte_offset} the tag’s position.

protobuf_nesting_exceeded.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Protobuf reason used when embedded messages nest deeper than the safety limit; {maximum_depth} is that limit (128 levels).

protobuf_no_fields.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Protobuf reason used when the value parses but contains no fields at all, so it is not treated as a message; fills {error} in the “not decodable as …, showing the hex dump” warning.

protobuf_summary_note.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: note shown after reading a value as Protobuf, warning that the tree shows raw field numbers and wire values because no schema (.proto definition) is available.
protobuf_summary_note.value: field numbers and wire values — no schema

protobuf_varint_overflow.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Protobuf reason used when a variable-length integer (varint, technical term) is longer than 64 bits allow; {byte_offset} is where it starts.

protobuf_varint_truncated.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: Protobuf reason used when a variable-length integer (varint, technical term) is cut off by the end of the value; {byte_offset} is where it starts.
protobuf_varint_truncated.value: varint at byte {byte_offset} runs past the end

raw_mode_button.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Tree/Raw switch: right segment, shown for JSON and XML values, that switches from the collapsible tree to the plain syntax-highlighted text.

remembered_formats_encode_failed.location: Results → Value viewer → Format memory: logged error when the list of remembered per-Redis-key display formats cannot be serialized for saving; {error} is the technical reason.
remembered_formats_encode_failed.value: Remembered value formats could not be encoded: {error}

remembered_formats_load_failed.location: Results → Value viewer → Format memory: error when the saved file of remembered per-Redis-key display formats is unreadable or corrupt; {error} is the reason; can appear in the Format note.
remembered_formats_load_failed.value: Remembered value formats could not be loaded: {error}

remembered_formats_save_failed.location: Results → Value viewer → Format memory: logged error when the remembered per-Redis-key display formats file cannot be written to disk; {error} is the technical reason.
remembered_formats_save_failed.value: Remembered value formats could not be saved: {error}

remembered_formats_session_only.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Format note: warning shown after picking a format for a Redis key when the remembered-formats file is unreadable; {error} is the load error; the choice lasts only for this session.
remembered_formats_session_only.value: {error}; this choice is kept for this session only.

sketch_mode_button.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Sketch/Raw switch: left segment, shown for geometry values, that draws the shape as a picture; noun or short label meaning a drawing.

spatial_raw_mode_button.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Sketch/Raw switch: right segment, shown for geometry values, that switches from the drawn shape to the raw geometry text (e.g. WKT).

spatial_search_placeholder.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar: placeholder of the search box created for geometry values (the box is only displayed in Tree mode, so it is rarely seen); short “Search”.

tree_copy_path.location: Results → Value viewer → Tree mode → Row actions: small button that appears when hovering a tree row, copying that node’s path (e.g. a JSON path) to the clipboard.

tree_copy_value.location: Results → Value viewer → Tree mode → Row actions: small button beside “Copy Path” on a hovered tree row with a value, copying that node’s value to the clipboard.

tree_display_truncated.location: Results → Value viewer → Tree mode: dim line at the bottom of the tree when more than 5,000 rows would be shown; {hidden_rows} is how many rows are left out of the display.
tree_display_truncated.value: … display truncated: {hidden_rows} more rows not shown

tree_mode_button.location: Results → Value viewer → Toolbar → Tree/Raw switch: left segment, shown for JSON and XML values, that shows the value as a collapsible, searchable tree of nodes.

tree_more_children.location: Results → Value viewer → Tree mode: placeholder row at the end of a node with more than 2,000 children; {hidden_count} is the number of children not listed; starts with an ellipsis.

tree_no_matches.location: Results → Value viewer → Tree mode: empty-state message in the tree area when the toolbar search text matches no node.

tree_search_placeholder.location: Results → Structured Data Viewer → normal tree constructor: search-field placeholder “Search” in the structured-data tree toolbar.

zstd_browser_unavailable.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used in the browser (web) version, where zstd decompression is not included, when zstd is picked; fills {error} in the “not decodable as …, showing the hex dump” warning.
zstd_browser_unavailable.value: zstd decoding is not available in the browser build

zstd_claimed_size_exceeds_cap.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when a zstd frame header announces a decompressed size over the limit, refused before decompressing; {claimed_bytes} is that size, {size_cap} the “the 16 MB cap” phrase.
zstd_claimed_size_exceeds_cap.value: the zstd frame header claims {claimed_bytes} bytes; {size_cap} refuses it

zstd_invalid_header.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when a value starts with the zstd magic bytes but its frame header is corrupt or cut short; fills {error} in the “not decodable as …, showing the hex dump” warning.
zstd_invalid_header.value: corrupt or truncated zstd frame header

zstd_missing_header.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when zstd is picked but the value does not start with the zstd magic bytes 28 b5 2f fd; fills {error} in the “not decodable as …, showing the hex dump” warning.
zstd_missing_header.value: no zstd frame header (28 b5 2f fd)

zstd_open_failed.location: Results → Value viewer → Format note → Decode failure reason: reason used when the zstd decompressor cannot be started for the value; {error} is its technical message, prefixed with the format name “zstd”.

browse_button.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Footer buttons: button at the left of the footer that opens a folder picker and fills the Output folder field with the chosen folder.

cli_copied_button.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Footer buttons: confirmation label that replaces “Copy CLI command” after the equivalent command line was copied to the clipboard; reverts once any option changes.

cli_copy_requirements.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog: inline error shown above the table list when Copy CLI command is clicked without an output folder, a checked table, or a format the command-line tool can write.
cli_copy_requirements.value: Copy CLI command needs an output folder, at least one table, and a CSV, TSV, JSON, JSON Lines, or Markdown format

copy_cli_button.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Footer buttons: button that copies an equivalent sqlly command-line invocation for the current choices to the clipboard; disabled for formats the CLI cannot write.

database_scope.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Description line: lowercase word filling the parenthesised scope in “Export tables from … (…)” when the dialog was opened on a whole database rather than one schema.

description.location: Results → Export Tables dialog: description identifying the source {database_name} and database or schema {scope}, and explaining that each selected table is exported separately.
description.value: Export tables from {database_name} ({scope}) to separate files.

dialog_title.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog: dialog title; {connection_name} is the name of the saved connection whose tables are listed for batch export to separate files.

filename_pattern_hint.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Filename pattern: small caption above the filename pattern input listing the tokens in double braces; {default_pattern} is the pattern used when the field is empty.

folder_required.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog: inline error shown above the table list when the export button is clicked while the Output folder field is empty.

format_label.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Format: small caption above the export file-format dropdown (CSV, JSON, Excel, …); its English text currently repeats the filename-pattern hint by mistake; it should name the format choice.

formula_protection.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Options: checkbox label; when checked, cell values starting with =, +, - or @ are prefixed with an apostrophe so spreadsheets do not run them as formulas.
formula_protection.value: Protect against spreadsheet formulas (prefix =, +, -, @ with an apostrophe)

gzip_files.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Options: checkbox label; when checked, each exported table file is written gzip-compressed.

include_header.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Options: checkbox label; when checked, each exported file starts with a row of column names.

line_breaks_escape.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Line breaks in cells dropdown: third option; writes line breaks inside cell values as escape sequences instead of real line breaks.

line_breaks_keep.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Line breaks in cells dropdown: first (default) option; leaves line breaks inside cell values unchanged in the exported files.

line_breaks_label.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Line breaks in cells: small caption above the dropdown choosing how line breaks inside cell values are written (keep, replace with space, escape).

line_breaks_space.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Line breaks in cells dropdown: second option; replaces each line break inside a cell value with a single space.

loading_tables.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Table list: placeholder shown in place of the table checkboxes while the dialog is still fetching the database’s tables.

no_tables.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Table list: empty-state message shown when the database or schema has no tables to export and no loading error occurred.

null_custom.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → NULL text dropdown: last option; shows a text field where the user types their own text to write for NULL values.

null_empty.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → NULL text dropdown: second option; writes NULL values as an empty cell.

null_format_default.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → NULL text dropdown: first (default) option; uses whatever NULL representation the chosen file format normally uses.

null_text_label.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → NULL text: small caption above the dropdown choosing what text represents NULL values in the exported files.

output_folder_label.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Output folder: small caption above the folder path input where the exported files are written (filled by Browse… or typed).

run_button.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Footer buttons: primary button that starts the export; plural form, {table_count} is the number of checked tables (0 or 2 and more).

run_button_one.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Footer buttons: primary button that starts the export; singular form used when exactly one table is checked ({table_count} is 1).

schema_scope.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Description line: lowercase phrase filling the parenthesised scope in “Export tables from … (…)” when opened on one schema; {schema_name} is that schema.

select_all_button.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Footer buttons: left-side button that checks every table in the list.

select_none_button.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog → Footer buttons: left-side button that unchecks every table in the list.

table_required.location: Object Explorer → Database or schema context menu → Export Tables dialog: inline error shown above the table list when the export button is clicked with no table checked.

always_mask_button.location: Results → Toolbar → Mask suggestion chips: second chip, shown when the AI decision model flags personal-looking columns; adds those columns to the global masking rules so they are masked in every result.
always_mask_button.value: Always mask these columns: add them to the global masking rules

always_mask_tooltip.location: Results → Toolbar → Mask suggestion chips: tooltip on the “Always mask” chip explaining that it adds the suggested columns to the global masking rules (Settings → Results → Masking).
always_mask_tooltip.value: Always mask these columns: add them to the global masking rules

dismiss_mask_suggestion_tooltip.location: Results → Toolbar → Mask suggestion chips: tooltip on the small × chip after the mask suggestion; hides the suggestion for the current result only.
dismiss_mask_suggestion_tooltip.value: Dismiss this suggestion for this result

mask_many_personal_columns.location: Results → Toolbar → Mask suggestion chips: chip label asking whether to mask columns the AI decision model thinks hold personal data; plural form, {column_count} is 2 or more.

mask_one_personal_column.location: Results → Toolbar → Mask suggestion chips: chip label asking whether to mask the single column the AI decision model thinks holds personal data; singular form.

mask_suggestion_tooltip.location: Results → Toolbar → Mask suggestion chips: tooltip on the “Mask N personal-looking columns?” chip; clicking masks those columns in the current result only.
mask_suggestion_tooltip.value: Columns whose values look personal — click to mask them for this result

masked_columns_tooltip.location: Results → Toolbar: tooltip on the shield icon chip shown while some result columns are masked; clicking reveals all masked values in the current result.
masked_columns_tooltip.value: Masked columns — click to reveal all for this result

multi_sort_tooltip.location: Results → Toolbar: tooltip on the chip listing the sort columns, shown when the grid is sorted by two or more columns; clicking removes the sort.

save_chart_library.location: Results → Toolbar: chip shown while the Chart tab is in front; opens the flow that saves this chart with its query to the Saved Charts library.

save_chart_library_tooltip.location: Results → Toolbar: tooltip on the “Save chart to library…” chip explaining that the chart layout and query are kept in Tools → Saved Charts and on the Chart Dashboard.
save_chart_library_tooltip.value: Keep this chart layout with its query in Tools > Saved Charts and on the Chart Dashboard

suggested_chart_revert.location: Results → Toolbar: chip shown while the Chart tab displays a layout chosen by the AI decision model; clicking reverts to the chart’s automatic detection. Short label, “·” separates two parts.

suggested_chart_tooltip.location: Results → Toolbar: tooltip on the “Suggested chart · Revert” chip explaining that the AI decision model picked the chart layout and clicking restores automatic detection.
suggested_chart_tooltip.value: This chart layout was suggested by the decision model — click to revert to automatic detection

complete_footer.location: Results → Grid context menu → Values → Top Values window: summary line at the top of the window after every row was counted; {counted_rows} is the number of rows counted. Clicking a listed value filters the grid column.
complete_footer.value: {counted_rows} rows counted. Click a value to filter this column to it.

counting_footer.location: Results → Grid context menu → Values → Top Values window: progress line at the top of the window while a large on-disk result is still being read; {row_count} is how many rows will be read.

empty_values.location: Results → Grid context menu → Values → Top Values window: empty-state message in the value list when the counted rows contain no values for this column.
empty_values.value: No values in the counted rows.

read_error.location: Results → Grid context menu → Values → Top Values window: error line at the top of the window when the result’s temporary on-disk copy (spill file) could not be read while counting.
read_error.value: The result's spill file could not be read — close this window and try again.

sampled_footer.location: Results → Grid context menu → Values → Top Values window: summary line at the top when only part of the rows were counted; {counted_rows} rows counted out of {total_rows} in the column. Clicking a value filters the grid column.
sampled_footer.value: Counted the first {counted_rows} of {total_rows} rows — counts are for those rows only. Click a value to filter this column to it.

stale_results.location: Results → Grid context menu → Values → Top Values window: message at the top of the window when the grid’s results were replaced (for example by re-running the query) while the window was open.
stale_results.value: These results were replaced — close this window and open Top Values again.

value_count.location: Results → Grid context menu → Values → Top Values window: occurrence count shown at the right of each value row; {count} is how many times the value appears. Keep it very short (× means “times”).

window_title.location: Results → Grid context menu → Values → Top Values window: title of the small separate window listing a column’s most frequent values; {column_name} is the grid column it counts.

complete_caption.location: Results → Grid context menu → Tools → Transpose: caption above the grid while the result is shown transposed; {row_count} is the number of original rows now shown as columns.

reading_rows.location: Results → Grid context menu → Tools → Transpose: caption above the grid while a large on-disk result is read before transposing; {row_count} is the number of rows being read.

source_column_header.location: Results → Grid context menu → Tools → Transpose: header of the first column in the transposed grid, which lists the original column names.

source_row_header.location: Results → Grid context menu → Tools → Transpose: header of each data column in the transposed grid; {row_number} is the 1-based number of the original row it shows.

truncated_caption.location: Results → Grid context menu → Tools → Transpose: caption above the grid when the result had more than 1,000 rows and only the first 1,000 were transposed; {row_count} is the number transposed.
truncated_caption.value: Transposed — {row_count} rows as columns — showing first 1,000 rows

error_disabled_or_renamed.location: Administration → Activity Monitor → Redis Slow Log: inline error shown when Redis does not recognize CONFIG; preserve the raw server detail.
error_disabled_or_renamed.value: CONFIG is disabled or renamed on this server: {detail}

error_failed.location: Administration → Activity Monitor → Redis Slow Log: generic inline error shown when reading the threshold fails; preserve the raw detail.

error_permission.location: Administration → Activity Monitor → Redis Slow Log: inline error shown when the Redis ACL refuses CONFIG GET; preserve the raw server detail.
error_permission.value: this user lacks permission to run CONFIG GET (+config|get): {detail}

lead_disabled.location: Administration → Activity Monitor → Redis Slow Log: leading status shown when the slow-log threshold is negative.

lead_threshold.location: Administration → Activity Monitor → Redis Slow Log: leading status showing the configured slow-log threshold with units.

lead_unknown.location: Administration → Activity Monitor → Redis Slow Log: leading status shown when the threshold cannot be read.

note_disabled.location: Administration → Activity Monitor → Redis Slow Log: caption explaining that logging is disabled and older retained commands are shown.
note_disabled.value: the slow log is disabled (slowlog-log-slower-than = {threshold_micros}) — showing up to the {command_limit} most recent commands recorded before

note_threshold.location: Administration → Activity Monitor → Redis Slow Log: caption describing the command limit and active threshold.
note_threshold.value: showing the {command_limit} most recent commands slower than {threshold}

note_unknown.location: Administration → Activity Monitor → Redis Slow Log: caption shown when commands are available but their threshold is unknown.
note_unknown.value: showing the {command_limit} most recent slow-log commands (the slowlog-log-slower-than threshold could not be read)

no_key_original_values.location: Administration → Transaction Preview → Primary Key Warning: warning shown when updates must use original values for conflict detection.
no_key_original_values.value: No primary key detected; generated updates use original-value conflict predicates.

no_key_read_only.location: Administration → Table Editing → Primary Key Warning: warning shown when no stable key permits editing.
no_key_read_only.value: Editing without a primary key is read-only until a stable key is selected.

backup_failed.location: Administration → Backup: error shown when a database backup fails; preserve the raw server detail.

not_supported.location: Administration tools → Capability error: message shown when the selected administrative operation is unsupported.

restore_failed.location: Administration → Restore: error shown when a database restore fails; preserve the raw server detail.

rank_avg_duration.location: Administration → Query Insights: ranking option that sorts queries by average execution duration.

rank_avg_reads.location: Administration → Query Insights: ranking option that sorts queries by average read activity.

rank_executions.location: Administration → Query Insights: ranking option that sorts queries by execution count.

action_failed.location: SQL Agent → Job Action Error: message shown when a job action fails; preserve the server detail.

job_not_found.location: SQL Agent → Job Error: message shown when the requested job no longer exists.

not_available.location: SQL Agent → Availability Error: message shown when the agent cannot be used; preserve the server detail.

agent_starts.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: recurrence text for a schedule triggered by agent startup.

computer_idle.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: recurrence text for a schedule triggered by computer idle time.

daily.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: recurrence text for a daily schedule.

every_days.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: recurrence text for a schedule repeating every several days.

monthly_day.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: recurrence text for a monthly day-of-month schedule.

monthly_relative.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: recurrence text for a relative monthly schedule.

once.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: recurrence text for a one-time schedule.

unknown.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: honest fallback showing raw frequency codes for an unknown recurrence.

friday.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: abbreviated Friday name in a weekly recurrence.

monday.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: abbreviated Monday name in a weekly recurrence.

saturday.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: abbreviated Saturday name in a weekly recurrence.

sunday.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: abbreviated Sunday name in a weekly recurrence.

thursday.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: abbreviated Thursday name in a weekly recurrence.

tuesday.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: abbreviated Tuesday name in a weekly recurrence.

wednesday.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: abbreviated Wednesday name in a weekly recurrence.

weekly.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: recurrence text for a weekly schedule without named weekdays.

weekly_days.location: SQL Agent → Schedules: recurrence text for a weekly schedule with separately localized weekdays.

egress_claude.location: AI → Local Agent → Privacy Notice: disclosure shown before enabling Claude Code agent mode.
egress_claude.value: Agent mode runs a local Claude Code CLI that talks to Anthropic's cloud; table names, column lists, sample rows and SELECT results pass through it.

egress_codex.location: AI → Local Agent → Privacy Notice: disclosure shown before enabling Codex agent mode.
egress_codex.value: Agent mode runs a local Codex CLI that talks to OpenAI's cloud; table names, column lists, sample rows and SELECT results pass through it.

corrupt.location: AI → Schema Catalog → Storage Error: message shown when the local catalog is corrupt; preserve the integrity-check detail.
corrupt.value: catalog file failed its integrity check: {detail}

newer_schema.location: AI → Schema Catalog → Compatibility Error: message shown when the catalog schema is newer than the app supports.
newer_schema.value: catalog was written by a newer app (schema generation {stamped}, this build supports {supported}); update the app

decode.location: AI → Decision Provider → Decode Error: message shown when the provider response cannot be decoded.
decode.value: could not decode decision provider response: {detail}

disabled.location: AI → Decision Provider → Availability Error: message shown when the decision provider is disabled.

invalid_request.location: AI → Decision Provider → Request Error: message shown when a decision request is invalid.

rate_limited.location: AI → Decision Provider → Rate Limit Error: message shown after the provider rate limits a request.
rate_limited.value: decision provider rate limited the request

status.location: AI → Decision Provider → HTTP Error: message shown for an unsuccessful provider response; preserve the response detail.

transport.location: AI → Decision Provider → Transport Error: message shown when the provider cannot be reached; preserve the detail.

dimension_mismatch.location: AI → Embeddings → Model Error: message shown when a model returns an unexpected embedding dimension.
dimension_mismatch.value: embedding dimension mismatch: model {model} expected {expected} dims but got {actual}

build.location: AI → Jev Provider → Client Error: message shown when the HTTP client cannot be constructed.
build.value: failed to build Jev HTTP client: {detail}

decode.location: AI → Jev Provider → Decode Error: message shown when the Jev response cannot be decoded.

rate_limited.location: AI → Jev Provider → Rate Limit Error: message shown after Jev rate limits a request.

status.location: AI → Jev Provider → HTTP Error: message shown for an unsuccessful Jev response; preserve the response detail.

transport.location: AI → Jev Provider → Transport Error: message shown when the Jev endpoint cannot be reached.

build.location: AI → MLX Provider → Client Error: message shown when the sidecar HTTP client cannot be constructed.
build.value: failed to build MLX HTTP client: {detail}

decode.location: AI → MLX Provider → Decode Error: message shown when the sidecar response cannot be decoded.
